class.name: EretheaHairStrands
class.brief_description: Hair drawn strand by strand, from a mesh of lines.
class.description: Draws hair from a mesh whose surfaces are lines ([constant Mesh.PRIMITIVE_LINES] or [constant Mesh.PRIMITIVE_LINE_STRIP]), such as the loose edges that Blender exports to glTF. Each strand is a chain of connected segments: a segment that starts where the previous one ended continues its strand, and any other segment starts a new strand. Surfaces that are not lines are ignored. The strands are turned into ribbons, two vertices per point, that a built-in shader opens towards the camera, tapering to the tip. Transparency uses alpha hash, so there is no sorting problem, and the shine has two anisotropic highlights (Kajiya-Kay). Bones and weights of the source vertices are copied, so the hair follows a [Skeleton3D]: make this node a child of the skeleton (or set [member MeshInstance3D.skeleton]) like any [MeshInstance3D]. The [member MeshInstance3D.mesh] is made from [member source_mesh] and is not saved with the scene. To use a shader of your own, set [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override]. The ribbons carry the strand direction in the tangent, the side ([code]-1[/code] or [code]1[/code]) and the position from root to tip in [code]UV[/code], and a random value per strand and the strand length in [code]UV2[/code]. [b]Note:[/b] The strands must be in order, root to tip. A segment drawn backwards in the middle of a strand starts a new strand.

method.name: get_source_strand_count
method.description: Returns the number of strands found in [member source_mesh], whatever the value of [member strand_fraction].

method.name: get_strand_count
method.description: Returns the number of strands that are drawn.

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Makes the ribbons from [member source_mesh] now. This is done by itself, at the end of the frame, when [member source_mesh], [member strand_fraction] or [member width] change.

members.member: How much light goes through the hair, seen against the light, as a fraction of the hair color.
Color of the hair at the root. The color goes from this to [member color_tip] along each strand, and varies a little from strand to strand.
Color of the hair at the tip.
Roughness of the hair, as in [member BaseMaterial3D.roughness].
The mesh of lines with the strands, for example the mesh imported from a glTF file with loose edges. It can have bones and weights, which are copied to the ribbons.
Strength of the narrow, white highlight.
Strength of the wide highlight, tinted by the hair color.
Moves the narrow highlight along the strand. Positive values move it towards the tip.
Moves the wide highlight along the strand.
Fraction of the strands that are drawn, spread evenly over the hair. Use it as a level of detail: [code]0.5[/code] draws every other strand. The width is not compensated.
Width of the strand at the tip, as a fraction of [member width].
Width of the strand at the root, in meters. The AABB used for culling includes half of it.
